newsitem.title: USA: Medtronic says first Jewel AF implanted.
newsitem.headline: Medtronic says first Jewel AF implanted.

text.p: Medtronic Inc said the first human implant was accomplished of the Jewel AF arrhythmia management device for detecting and treating heart rhythm disturbances, including atrial and ventricular fibrillation.
At 55 cc's displacement and 93 grams in weight, the device is one of the smallest and lightest defibrillators in the world, Medtronic said.
The implantation took place in Germany on January 10 in a 61-year-old woman suffering from atrial flutter and fibrillation, as well as ventricular tachycardia, it said.

European clinical investigations under way will evaluate the device's performance for patients with a combination of ventricular arrhythmias and atrial fibrillation. Evaluations will begin in the United States when authorized by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, Medtronic said.
Evaluations under a protocol including persons with atrial fibrillation only are also planned, it said.
